airdrops.name: TxFlow
airdrops.shortDesc: Layer-1 orderbook & parallel execution ecosystem built around shared liquidity channels.
airdrops.analysis: TxFlow is an on-chain trading and Layer-1 execution environment focused on shared liquidity across perpetuals, spot markets, and prediction channels. Participants typically earn points by bridging USDC, maintaining consistent weekly perpetuals volume, and testing spot pairs. Key risks include smart-contract risk on a newer execution layer, trading fees exceeding potential token rewards if over-leveraged, and dilution if total points supply expands sharply before TGE. Always use a dedicated farming wallet and verify official contract addresses before signing transactions.

Avoid excessive leverage, as liquidation losses outweigh any potential airdrop allocation.

guides.title: Wallet Security Rules for Airdrop Farming
guides.summary: How to isolate farming wallets, revoke risky token approvals, and avoid phishing claims.
guides.body: Never use your primary hardware vault for unverified testnets or new airdrop protocols. Create a dedicated browser profile and fresh EVM/Solana addresses funded only with the gas and capital you intend to test. Bookmark official domains directly rather than clicking sponsored search ads or unverified social replies. Regularly audit and revoke unlimited ERC-20 token approvals, and remember that no legitimate claim portal will ever ask for your 12-word or 24-word recovery phrase.

guides.title: How Crypto Points Convert Into Token Airdrops
guides.summary: Understanding FDV, airdrop pool percentages, linear vs. tiered distributions, and dilution.
guides.body: Most modern protocols use off-chain points programs to measure user activity before Token Generation Event (TGE). Your potential share depends on four variables: expected Fully Diluted Valuation (FDV) at launch, the percentage of total token supply allocated to the community pool, total points emitted before the snapshot, and whether the project applies linear distribution or anti-sybil minimum thresholds. Always model conservative FDV scenarios so trading fees never exceed realistic rewards.

guides.title: Risks of Perpetual DEX Airdrop Farming
guides.summary: Why fee drag, funding rates, and liquidation risk matter more than raw volume.
guides.body: Chasing leaderboard volume on perpetual DEXs can quickly result in net losses if taker fees and negative funding rates exceed token value. Prefer maker limit orders where fee rebates apply, keep leverage conservative (1x-5x) to avoid liquidation wicks, and track your cumulative fees paid against estimated points earned.
